study type: secondary analysis of a randomized controlled trial
cohort: 670 women with monochorionic-diamniotic twin pregnancies from the Twin Birth Study
finding: In monochorionic-diamniotic twin pregnancies between 32 weeks and 0 to 7 days of gestation and 38 weeks and 6 to 7 days of gestation, with twin A in a cephalic presentation, planned cesarean delivery did not decrease or increase the risk of fetal or neonatal death or serious neonatal morbidity, as compared with planned vaginal delivery.
mod_finding: In monochorionic-diamniotic twin pregnancies between 32 and 38 weeks of gestation, with twin A in cephalic presentation, planned cesarean delivery did not decrease or increase the risk of adverse perinatal outcomes compared to planned vaginal delivery.
gest_age: 32 weeks and 0 days gestation to 38 weeks and 6 days gestation
